title: quantum-group: Exact SymPy verification of explicit U_q(sl_2) and GL_q(2|1) matrix identities

creators.name: Terekli, Taha Berk
creators.affiliation: Department of Mathematics, Yıldız Technical University, Istanbul, Türkiye

description:
quantum-group is a small Python package that builds the explicit matrices behind concrete quantum-group calculations with exact SymPy arithmetic and checks each identity as an exact residual matrix. A nonzero residual entry locates the convention that disagrees: basis order, tensor placement, coproduct or, for superalgebras, the Koszul sign rule.

Covered: finite-dimensional Uq(sl2) modules and their defining relations; coproduct, counit and antipode with generator-level Hopf identities; tensor products and Clebsch–Gordan highest-weight vectors; the fundamental R-matrix with quantum Yang–Baxter, braid, Hecke and coproduct-intertwining checks, in the historical and the coproduct-compatible convention; and the graded Yang–Baxter equation for the 9×9 GLq(2|1) R-matrix of Çelik and Çelik (2021), including Rij placements on tensor powers via graded swaps.

Scope: the checks are exact verifications on explicit finite-dimensional representations, not proofs in the abstract algebra, and the package is not a general quantum-group computer algebra system.

This release (1.1.1) has the same package code and test suite as 1.1.0 (10.5281/zenodo.23015576). It adds the userguide prepared for SciPost Physics Codebases (scipost/; the same text as an amsart preprint in arxiv/), its worked examples with stored expected outputs, and a cross-check against data exported from GAP's QuaGroup package; continuous integration runs every example and compares its output. Earlier journal-submission records, the thesis poster and rendered page images are kept in the repository but are left out of this archive.

Install: pip install quantum-group==1.1.1. Validate: python -m pytest (202 tests and doctests). Requires Python ≥ 3.10, SymPy ≥ 1.10, NetworkX ≥ 2.6, Matplotlib ≥ 3.5. Source, documentation and issues: github.com/TerekliTahaBerk/quantum-groups.
